question: What is the relationship between interest rate and demand for money?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Inverse**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Interest rates bear an inverse relationship with the demand for money.
 
• Opportunity costs of holding money will be high when interest rates are high;
 
 
• people are losing out on possible earnings that interest-bearing investments could have generated.
 
• When interest rates are high, the opportunity cost of holding money increases because people can earn more by investing their money rather than keeping it as cash.
 
• This leads to a **lower demand for money** for transactional and speculative purposes
 
 
 
• When interest rates are low, the opportunity cost of holding money is low.
 
• People prefer holding more money for transactions or precautionary needs because the benefit of investing it is minimal.
 
• This leads to a higher demand for money.
 
• The relationship can be visualized using the liquidity preference theory by John Maynard Keynes:
 
• The demand for money (liquidity preference) decreases as the interest rate increases, and vice versa.
